WITH s AS (
  SELECT sku, sum(units_sold) units, sum(revenue_inr) rev FROM store.daily_sales GROUP BY sku
), w AS (
  SELECT sku, sum(units) woff_units,
         sum(units * (SELECT cost_inr FROM store.products p WHERE p.sku=w.sku)) woff_cost,
         sum(units) FILTER (WHERE reason='expired') expired_units,
         sum(units) FILTER (WHERE reason='damaged') damaged_units
  FROM store.write_offs w GROUP BY sku
), a AS (
  SELECT sku, count(*) audits, sum((status='empty')::int) empties FROM store.shelf_audits GROUP BY sku
), z AS (
  SELECT sku, sum((units_sold=0)::int) zero_sales_days, count(*) days FROM store.daily_sales GROUP BY sku
), b AS (
  SELECT sku, sum((book_on_hand_close<=0)::int) zero_book_days, count(*) days FROM store.inventory_book GROUP BY sku
)
SELECT p.sku, p.name, p.flow, p.price_inr, p.cost_inr,
       s.units, s.rev, round(s.rev - s.units*p.cost_inr,2) gross_profit,
       round((s.rev - s.units*p.cost_inr)/nullif(s.rev,0)*100,2) gross_margin_pct,
       w.woff_units, w.expired_units, w.damaged_units, round(w.woff_cost,2) woff_cost,
       round(w.woff_units::numeric/nullif(s.units,0)*100,2) woff_pct_of_sales,
       a.audits, a.empties, z.zero_sales_days, b.zero_book_days
FROM store.products p
JOIN s ON s.sku=p.sku
LEFT JOIN w ON w.sku=p.sku
LEFT JOIN a ON a.sku=p.sku
LEFT JOIN z ON z.sku=p.sku
LEFT JOIN b ON b.sku=p.sku
ORDER BY woff_pct_of_sales DESC NULLS LAST, s.units DESC;

**Q1 — Range decisions (add/drop):** *proxy.* No record holds a range decision (no assortment plan, no candidate new products, no delisting decisions). Stand-in signals from the June records: **review/drop candidates** — MILK-FC-500ML (198 units written off, all expired = 6.8% of its units sold; 6 days sold while book stock ≤ 0), MILK-TONED-500ML (296 units written off, 291 expired = 3.4% of units sold), ATTA-WW-5KG (2 of 8 shelf audits empty, 4 zero-sales days while books showed stock, forecast ran 11% above actual sales). **Add candidates: no record** — all 11 catalog SKUs sold in June, so there is no evidence of unmet demand for a product not in the range.

**Q2 — Supplier payment terms and working capital:** *no record.* There is no supplier invoice, purchase-order value, due date, credit-period, payables or receivables ledger anywhere in `store`, `warehouse` or `payments`; the only payment-terms-like fields are UPI settlement columns (`gross_inr`, `refunds_inr`, `mdr_inr`, `net_inr`). Working capital (current assets minus current liabilities) therefore cannot be computed — no record.

**Q3 — Payment complaints in June 2026:** **26** (23 "charged twice", 3 "debited but the till said failed"); all 26 complaint rows fall in June 2026.

**Q4 — Profitability in June 2026:** *proxy.* Revenue ₹1,243,937, COGS ₹1,107,731.10 → **gross profit ₹136,205.90 (10.95% margin)**; after write-offs (₹15,269.10) and customer refunds (₹11,301.86) ≈ ₹109,634.94 before operating costs. Rent, salaries, utilities and other opex are not recorded, so net/overall profitability cannot be confirmed — only that trading is gross-profitable.

**Q5 — Shelf-audit rows showing empty in June 2026:** **3** (SUGAR-1KG on 5 Jun; ATTA-WW-5KG on 12 Jun and 26 Jun).

**Q6 — Products sold:** **11** distinct SKUs (identical in `store.products`, `store.daily_sales` and `store.pos_lines` for June).

**Q7 — Cashier productivity:** *no record.* No table carries a cashier/till/operator/lane identifier (`pos_lines`, `pos_payments` have only bill, attempt, tender, status, RRN), so per-cashier throughput cannot be attributed.

**Q8 — Price elasticity for 5 kg atta:** *no record.* ATTA-WW-5KG sold at a single price of ₹265.00 across all 1,177 till lines (4 May–28 Jun) and every June daily-sales row implies ₹265.00; with no price variation there is no demand response to measure.

## Final answers

**Q1 — Toor dal batch/lot for a recall: no record.**
There is no batch/lot field anywhere in the database (the only column names matching "lot" are `slot`/`dc_slot`/`slot_start`/`slot_end`), and no quality-issue, complaint or recall record for toor dal. The only toor-dal stock event is a "damaged" write-off that names no lot, so no lot can be identified for a recall.

**Q2 — Weather/festivals/local events and June sales: no record.**
No weather, festival, holiday or local-event table or column exists (the only regex hit was `payments.pos_payments.attempt`). Daily sales by SKU are recorded, but nothing to attribute changes to, so no causal statement is possible.

**Q3 — Profit-maximising price for toned milk 500 ml: no record.**
Only one price was ever charged for the SKU (₹26, cost ₹24.7) across all 35,485 till lines; there is no price variation, elasticity, promotion or price-response record, so a profit-maximising price cannot be derived.

**Q4 — June true demand for toned milk 500 ml: proxy ≈ 8,745 units.**
Actual June sales were 8,649 units. Applying the store's own forecast method ("28-day mean of recorded sales", used in `store.forecasts` for the DC SKUs) day by day gives 8,744.5 units of demand, i.e. ≈909 units of unmet demand. The estimate is conservative: on 2–3 June book stock closed at 5 and 7 units yet sales still exceeded the base, and no lost-sale/demand record exists.

**Q5 — Best customers by June spend: no record.**
No customer identifier (customer id, membership, phone, card) exists in any of the 21 tables; `pos_lines`/`pos_payments` carry only `bill_id`, so spend cannot be attributed to a customer.

**Q6 — Food-safety and labelling compliance: partially compliant, with material control gaps.**
- Labelling/identification: all 11 products carry a GTIN matching the SHACL pattern (0 invalid), and all 35,485 till lines have a `gtin_scanned` matching the product's GTIN (0 mismatches, 0 nulls) — item-level traceability is complete.
- Food safety: 19 expired write-off lines (489 units, of which 292 are toned milk) and 15 damaged units; 3 shelf-audit lines recorded "empty" (sugar 1 kg on 5 June, atta 5 kg on 12 June, one further line); fresh deliveries all arrive before use-by (0 expired on arrival).
- Control gaps: 0 of 70 picks confirmed by pack-code scan (all 70 by slot-label scan, Rule 7); 0 of 70 goods receipts checked case-by-case by pack code (all by pallet SSCC scan, Rule 8); 30 of 30 pallets "not weighed"; stock-count variances of 406 units absolute (incl. +157 on atta 1 kg and a zero count on atta 5 kg on 26 June) and warehouse adjustments of 224 units (−160 short-pick, +64 cycle-count).

**Q7 — New-product launch cannibalisation: no record.**
No launch date exists for any product, and all 11 SKUs were already selling from the first till day (4 May 2026); no SKU first sold after 1 June, so there is no June launch to test against an existing product.

**Q8 — Cost to serve cash vs UPI vs card: proxy (UPI only).**
Only UPI has a recorded cost: `upi_settlements.mdr_inr` is 0.00 on every settlement day, and refunds total ₹11,301.86 across 23 refunds in June 2026 (all triggered by customer complaints). No cash-handling cost and no card MDR/acquirer-fee record exist, so cash and card cost to serve cannot be computed.

## Final answers

**Q1 — Which product earns the most per square foot of shelf at Store 014?**
SQL: `SELECT table_schema, table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND (column_name ~* 'sqft|sq_ft|square|space|shelf|facings|brand|private|label');` (plus `SELECT * FROM store.products;`)
**Answer: no record.** The database has no shelf-area, facings, or square-foot field anywhere (no views either); `store.products` holds only sku/gtin/name/pack/case_units/case_kg/flow/dc_slot/price/cost. Revenue per product is recorded, but the denominator (shelf space) is not, so "per square foot" cannot be computed.
*Sure: high — this is a schema-wide absence, not a data gap.*

**Q2 — Write-off lines in June 2026 with reason 'expired'**
SQL: `SELECT reason, count(*) AS lines, sum(units) AS units FROM store.write_offs WHERE date >= DATE '2026-06-01' AND date < DATE '2026-07-01' GROUP BY reason;`
**Answer: 19 lines** (489 units; the other 15 lines are 'damaged').
*Sure: high — direct count on `store.write_offs`.*

**Q3 — What a customer's bank statement showed for a failed UPI payment in June 2026**
SQL: `SELECT pp.till_status, pr.status, count(*), sum(pp.amount_inr), sum(pr.amount_inr) FROM payments.pos_payments pp LEFT JOIN payments.psp_upi_report pr ON pr.rrn=pp.rrn WHERE pp.tender='UPI' AND pp.till_status IN ('failed','failed: no response','declined') GROUP BY 1,2;` plus the complaint join.
**Answer: no debit.** For all 145 UPI attempts the till marked 'failed' (₹86,750.06), the UPI/PSP record shows status `failed` — the bank statement shows no debit. For 48 attempts the till timed out ('failed: no response', ₹22,644.07) there is **no UPI record at all**, so the bank statement is not known yet (Rule 9: timeout ≠ failure). In 3 complaint cases ('debited but the till said failed', ₹667.30) the customer *was* debited and the bank returned the money (UPI status `returned`).
*Sure: high for the failed/no-debit reading; the 48 timeouts are explicitly "not known yet", not failures.*

**Q4 — Why do shoppers choose cash, card or UPI?**
SQL: `SELECT tender, count(*) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved'), sum(amount_inr) FILTER (WHERE till_status='approved') FROM payments.pos_payments GROUP BY tender;`
**Answer: no record.** The records hold only the tender mix and per-tender outcomes (UPI dominant, then cash, then card; card declines and UPI declines/timeouts are visible). There is no customer, reason, promotion, fee or preference field anywhere, so the *drivers* of tender choice are not recorded.
*Sure: high — no motivation/driver attribute exists in any table.*

**Q5 — How much should expiring milk be marked down to sell through before its use-by date?**
SQL: `SELECT * FROM store.fresh_deliveries WHERE sku LIKE 'MILK%' ORDER BY delivery_ts LIMIT 15;` and `SELECT reason, count(*), sum(units) FROM store.write_offs GROUP BY reason;`
**Answer: no record.** The records hold use-by dates on fresh deliveries, list price/cost, and expired write-offs (19 lines, 489 units in June), but there is no markdown, price-change, discount-policy or elasticity record — so no markdown amount can be derived without inventing a demand curve.
*Sure: high — no pricing-decision table or price history exists.*

**Q6 — Do shoppers prefer brands or private label?**

**Q1 — Were Store 014's fresh products kept cold in transit in June 2026?**
SQL: `SELECT count(*) AS fresh_delivery_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE delivery_ts::time <> '05:30:00') AS off_window, min(use_by - delivery_ts::date) AS min_shelf_life_days, max(use_by - delivery_ts::date) AS max_shelf_life_days FROM store.fresh_deliveries WHERE delivery_ts >= '2026-06-01' AND delivery_ts < '2026-07-01';` and `SELECT table_name, column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema IN ('store','warehouse','payments') AND column_name ~* 'temp|cold|reef|chill';`
**Answer: no record.** The only fresh-delivery record (112 rows, routes R‑07/R‑12, all arriving 05:30, use‑by 1–3 days out) carries no temperature, reefer or cold‑chain field, and no such column exists anywhere in the database, so transit temperature cannot be checked.
*Confidence: high — the absence of any temperature/cold-chain attribute is verified against the full schema; the 497 expired/damaged DSD write-off units say nothing about transit temperature.*

**Q2 — How much of Store 014's payment volume in June 2026 was fraud?**
SQL: `WITH jp AS (SELECT * FROM payments.pos_payments WHERE ts >= '2026-06-01' AND ts < '2026-07-01'), dbl AS (SELECT amount_inr FROM payments.customer_complaints WHERE kind='charged twice' AND complaint_ts>='2026-06-01' AND complaint_ts<'2026-07-01') SELECT (SELECT sum(amount_inr) FROM jp WHERE till_status='approved') AS approved_volume, (SELECT count(*) FROM dbl) AS dbl_cases, (SELECT sum(amount_inr) FROM dbl) AS dbl_amount, (SELECT sum(amount_inr) FROM payments.customer_complaints WHERE kind='debited but the till said failed' AND complaint_ts>='2026-06-01' AND complaint_ts<'2026-07-01') AS till_failed_amount, (SELECT count(*) FROM payments.psp_upi_report WHERE status='returned') AS returned_debits, (SELECT sum(amount_inr) FROM payments.psp_upi_report WHERE status='returned') AS returned_amount;`
**Answer (proxy): ≈0.07% of June payment volume — ₹12,958.69 of ₹17,570,666.87 approved volume.** No record classifies anything as fraud; the stand-in is debits that were later reversed or refunded: 23 "charged twice" complaints (₹11,301.86, all refunded) plus 6 bank-"returned" debits (₹1,656.83, of which 3 were complained about).
*Confidence: medium — the proxy is well evidenced (complaints + refunds + PSP final status), but "fraud" itself is not a recorded category; these are wrongful/duplicate debits, not proven fraud.*

**Q7 — How many truck shipments arrived from the warehouse in June 2026?**

**Q8 — For how many hours in June 2026 was 5 kg atta off the shelf?**

**Answer (proxy): ≈44.1 hours minimum confirmed off the shelf** (empty audit 06‑12 11:00 → next sale 06‑13 10:43 = 23.7 h; empty audit 06‑26 11:00 → next sale 06‑27 07:22 = 20.4 h). Upper bound ≈137.4 h if the shelf emptied right after the last sale before each audit (06‑11 09:30 and 06‑23 15:10); book stock also sat at 63 units with zero sales on 06‑24/25 before the 06‑26 count found 0.
*Confidence: medium-low — availability is only observed at 8 point-in-time shelf audits plus sales; there is no continuous on-shelf record, so the true duration is a bounded estimate, not a measurement.*

## Final answers

**1. How many staff does Store 014 need in each hour of the day?**
SQL: none (explored `information_schema.tables`/`columns` for staff, roster, shift, labour tables — none exist).
**Answer: no record.** There is no staffing, roster, shift, labour-cost or till-queue table anywhere in `store`, `warehouse` or `payments`. Transaction volumes per hour exist (e.g. `pos_lines.bill_ts`, `pos_payments.ts`), but they cannot be turned into a headcount requirement without a service-level target (e.g. target customers per cashier-hour), which is also not recorded. Any number would be a guess.

**2. How many shoppers abandoned a basket at the till in June 2026?**
SQL: `SELECT count(DISTINCT bill_id) ... FROM store.pos_lines WHERE bill_ts >= '2026-06-01' AND bill_ts < '2026-07-01'` plus payment-status checks.
**Answer: no record.** A basket abandonment is a customer who presented items and left without paying. The records hold only completed bills: every one of the 13,851 June bills in `pos_lines` has a matching `pos_payments` row and an approved payment (0 bills without an approved payment). Failed/declined attempts (393 bills had a failed attempt before approval) are still paid bills, not abandonments. There is no basket/void/abandonment event table, so the count of abandonments is not recorded.

**3. How many distinct bills were rung up at the tills in June 2026?**
SQL: `SELECT count(DISTINCT bill_id) FROM store.pos_lines WHERE bill_ts >= '2026-06-01' AND bill_ts < '2026-07-01';`
**Answer: 13,851.** This is the count of distinct bill numbers in the till-lines record (`store.pos_lines`, the record that "looks at the shelf" per the ontology) for June 2026. Note `payments.pos_payments` shows 30,077 distinct bill IDs for the same month, but 16,226 of those have no till lines at all and their bill IDs run to ~140,000/day versus ~500–650/day in the till lines, so the till-lines record is the authoritative "bills rung up" source for Store 014.

**4. Where should the chain open its next store?**
SQL: none (searched all tables in `store`, `warehouse`, `payments` for site/store/market/location data — none exist).
**Answer: no record.** There is no site, GLN, catchment, competitor, demographic, rent, or chain-location table in the database; `store.products.dc_slot` is a warehouse slot code, not a location. The records contain no basis for choosing a new city or site.

**5. How many units were written off as expired in June 2026?**
SQL: `SELECT sum(units) FROM store.write_offs WHERE reason = 'expired' AND date >= '2026-06-01' AND date < '2026-07-01';`
**Answer: 489 units** (19 write-off rows with reason `expired`, 5–28 June). The other 15 write-off rows are `damaged` (15 units) and are excluded.

**6. How good are Store 014's shelf audits themselves (who audited, how, with what evidence)?**
SQL: `SELECT status, count(*), count(DISTINCT sku), min(audit_ts), max(audit_ts) FROM store.shelf_audits GROUP BY 1;` plus `SELECT * FROM store.shelf_audits WHERE status <> 'on shelf';`
**Answer: no record** for the audit-quality question itself. `store.shelf_audits` has only `audit_ts`, `sku`, `status` — there is no auditor identity, no method (scan vs. visual), no count/quantity, no evidence field, and no second observer, so "who audited, how, with what evidence" cannot be answered. What the records do show: 88 audit rows over 8 dates (2, 5, 9, 12, 16, 19, 23, 26 June), all at exactly 11:00, covering all 11 SKUs each time; 85 "on shelf" and 3 "empty" (SUGAR-1KG on 5 June; ATTA-WW-5KG on 12 and 26 June). The fixed 11:00 timestamp and single status per SKU per day suggest a scheduled snapshot rather than an independent, evidenced audit.

**7. What was the total net UPI amount settled to Store 014 in June 2026, in rupees?**
SQL: `SELECT sum(net_inr) FROM payments.upi_settlements WHERE settlement_date >= '2026-06-01' AND settlement_date < '2026-07-01';`
**Answer: ₹10,787,291.92** (29 daily settlement rows, 2–30 June; gross ₹10,798,593.78 less refunds ₹11,301.86, MDR ₹0). This reconciles with the PSP report: 18,410 successful UPI credits totalling ₹10,798,593.78.

**8. How satisfied are Store 014's customers?**
SQL: complaint/refund aggregation queries over `payments.customer_complaints` and `payments.upi_refunds`.
**Answer: no record** for satisfaction. There is no survey, CSAT/NPS, rating, or sentiment table. The only customer-voice records are 26 complaints (all resolved; 23 "charged twice", 3 "debited but the till said failed"; ₹11,969.16 involved) and 23 refunds (all completed; average refund turnaround 77.2 hours, average complaint resolution 71.2 hours). These are payment-failure proxies, not satisfaction measures — 1.88 complaints per 1,000 till bills — and cannot be reported as a satisfaction score.

## Final answers

**Q1 — Carbon footprint of Store 014's deliveries: no record.**
The database holds delivery logistics (vehicle `TRK-07`, routes `R-07`/`R-12`, pallet `notice_kg`, dispatch/arrival times) but no fuel, distance, vehicle-emission-factor or CO₂e fields anywhere in `store`, `warehouse` or `payments`. Tonnes moved could be computed, but converting that to carbon needs emission factors that are not recorded. No number given.

**Q2 — Comparison with the chain's other stores: no record.**
There is no `store_id`/site column in any table; every table contains only Store 014's data (one product catalogue, one till, one warehouse). No peer-store records exist, so no comparison is possible.

**Q3 — Sales at Diwali 2026: no record.**
Diwali 2026 falls in November 2026. The sales record ends 2026-06-28 (`daily_sales`, `pos_lines`) and the forecast record ends 2026-06-28 as well; there is no November history, no seasonality/event calendar and no forward forecast beyond June. No number given.

**Q4 — Gross margin on 5 kg atta, June 2026: proxy only (13.96%, ₹20,979).**
Real purchase costs, rebates and freight are **not** recorded — there is no purchase-cost, invoice, rebate or freight table; `products.cost_inr` (₹228/pack) is a static standard cost. Using it as a stand-in: revenue ₹150,255 on 567 packs, cost ₹129,276, margin ₹20,979 = **13.96%**. The true landed margin will differ by whatever rebates/freight the books do not hold.

**Q5 — Repeat rate and churn: no record.**
No customer identifier exists: `pos_lines` carries only `bill_id` (27,760 distinct bills over 56 days, none spanning more than one day), and there is no customer/member/loyalty table. Repeat visits cannot be attributed to a customer, so neither repeat rate nor churn can be computed.

**Q6 — June 2026 forecast accuracy for 5 kg atta: proxy (scored against sales, not demand).**
There is no demand record (no `Demand`/lost-sale table), so per Rule 4 the forecast cannot be scored against real demand. Scored against recorded sales as a stand-in: forecast 637.32 packs vs 567 sold, bias **+70.32 packs (+12.40% over-forecast)**, MAE 10.44 packs/day, WAPE **51.54%** over 28 days. Note the bias is overstated: on 12 Jun and 24–26 Jun the shelf was audited empty (0 sold) and book stock hit 0, so true demand exceeded sales.

**Q7 — Substitution when toned milk was empty: no record.**
Toned milk was never recorded as empty: all 15 shelf audits for `MILK-TONED-500ML` say "on shelf", and book stock never fell to ≤0 (minimum 5). (Full-cream milk's *believed* stock went negative on 6 days, but audits still showed it on shelf.) With no empty-toned-milk event, no substitution pattern is recorded.
